subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & VPC networking clarifications
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up — VPC networking asks

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and a focused set of asks so we can qualify the VPC path (Private VPC / PrivateLink or VPC Peering) vs Dedicated/Hosted options.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- FinTechX is leaning towards a private deployment for production traffic due to data residency and egress controls.
- Primary constraint: strict allowlist and no public-facing IPs for inference traffic.
- Team ownership: Alex (network), procurement (contracts), and security (policy).

High-level options (we touched on these):
1) Hosted API — fastest to ship but requires allowlisting Redwood egress IPs (not ideal given your posture).
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPUs in Redwood’s tenancy; still requires controlled egress but can be isolated per-tenant.
3) Private VPC (recommended given requirements) — Redwood Private control plane + PrivateLink or cross-account peering to keep traffic on your VPC boundaries.

To move forward on Private VPC qualification, can you confirm the following items? If you prefer, paste answers into the attached network template and send back. (Attachment: network-requirements-template.xlsx)

Critical asks for our network team:
- Preferred connectivity model: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) or VPC Peering/Transit? If you have a security preference, tell us why.
- VPC CIDR you’d like us to consider for routing (example: 10.12.0.0/16) and any subnet restrictions.
- Whether you require AWS Private DNS for the interface endpoint (yes/no).
- Do you allow inbound cross-account peering? Any org-level peering restrictions?
- Required allowlist format: CIDR ranges, FQDNs, or both? If CIDRs, do you have a place to accept a stable list of Redwood egress IPs?
- Any proxy/NAT or TLS inspection that could break mTLS/ALPN negotiation?

What Redwood will provide next once we confirm model and region:
- Stable egress IPs (if peering/egress allowlist required) per-region and per-environment.
- PrivateLink service name and recommended DNS entries.
- A short technical checklist and a 45-minute network call for hands-on setup.

Next steps suggested:
- Alex, if you can populate the attached template by EOD Thu 3/31 we’ll route to our infra team and propose a network call on Tue 4/5.
- We’ll cc our infra lead (Karthik) for technical details.

Thanks — attaching a short overview of Redwood Private networking to give your security folks context.

(Attachment: redwood-privatenet-overview.pdf)

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — VPC networking asks

Ben — thanks for the summary and the materials. Quick responses inline and attached our network template. (Attachment: network-requirements-template.xlsx)

- Connectivity model: Security prefers PrivateLink (interface endpoints) to avoid exposing any routes into our VPC via peering. PrivateLink reduces blast radius and aligns with our security standards.
- VPC CIDR: 10.12.0.0/16 (primary). We can allocate a /24 for endpoints if needed.
- Private DNS: yes, we prefer AWS Private DNS for name resolution and to avoid public DNS leakage.
- Cross-account peering: currently disallowed by org policy unless approved by our cloud platform team (we'd rather avoid that approval step).
- Allowlist format: we can do both FQDN (preferred for maintenance) and CIDR fallback for legacy rules. If you can provide stable egress CIDRs per-region that helps.
- TLS inspection: currently we have a TLS interception appliance in some envs. For production VPCs we can disable TLS inspection for PrivateLink traffic, but will need instructions to ensure proper certificate validation.

Notes: our security team will want the PrivateLink service name and a certificate SAN verification before we approve. Also looping procurement to start the legal checklist.

Alex Johnson
Sr. Network Engineer, FinTechX
alex.johnson@fintechx.com
(Attachment: network-requirements-template.xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — VPC networking asks

Alex — thanks for the quick answers and for attaching the template. A few technical clarifications from infra/networking that should help your security team and make the setup straightforward. See short answers below and a one-page quicksheet attached. (Attachment: privatelink-setup-quicksheet.pdf)

Quoted for context:
> - Connectivity model: Security prefers PrivateLink (interface endpoints) to avoid exposing any routes into our VPC via peering.

Short answers / notes:
- PrivateLink vs Peering: PrivateLink is our recommended default for customers who cannot accept peered routes. It keeps traffic inside AWS and terminates at an interface endpoint in your account. Peering is supported and can offer slightly lower latency in some topologies, but requires cross-account route management and is subject to your org restrictions.
- Ports/protocols: Only outbound HTTPS (443) is required for API traffic. If you plan to use model rollout telemetry or tracing, we may ask for additional outbound destinations — we’ll call these out explicitly if needed.
- DNS: If you enable Private DNS for the interface endpoint we will publish a service name like com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxxx and recommend a CNAME or route53 private hosted zone mapping. We’ll provide the exact FQDN and the TLS SAN for verification.
- Egress IPs: For PrivateLink, you don’t need to allowlist egress IPs for inbound traffic because the connection is via an interface endpoint in your VPC. For outbound-only allowlists (if you choose peering or Hosted API) we’ll provide a small set of stable CIDRs per region.
- TLS inspection: PrivateLink preserves TLS. If your appliance terminates TLS before the endpoint, certificate pinning and SAN checks may fail. For the production VPC we recommend bypassing TLS interception for the endpoint ENIs or using TCP passthrough.
- Health checks & ALBs: No inbound health-check ports are required from the customer side for PrivateLink; Redwood manages the backend.

Next practical steps we can do this week:
1) We’ll draft the PrivateLink service name and the FQDN + TLS SAN by EOD Wed 3/31 once Ben confirms region (you mentioned us-west-2 on the call).
2) If you’re open, schedule a 45-minute hands-on network session for Tue 4/5 — we’ll walk through the endpoint creation and DNS.
3) If procurement needs it, we can provide a short network design snippet for legal/security to attach to the contract.

Ben — happy to jump on the call as well.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
(Attachment: privatelink-setup-quicksheet.pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Alex — perfect, thanks for confirming. Short final note and proposed plan:

- We’ll proceed with PrivateLink in us-west-2 as the default for production based on your preference. Karthik will send the service name + FQDN + TLS SAN by EOD today so your security team can pre-approve.
- Please disable TLS inspection for the endpoint ENIs in the production VPC or allow TCP passthrough per Karthik’s note.
- Proposed hands-on session: Tue 4/5 at 10:00 AM PT — Karthik, Laura and I will join. Alex, procurement if that works for you we’ll book a calendar invite and include a short agenda (50% setup, 30% DNS cert/playbook, 20% Q&A & next steps).
- Deliverables from Redwood after the call: private service name, DNS entries, configuration checklist, and a checklist for procurement (SLA/contract points).

I’ve attached the overview again for your security team and the filled template you returned.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
